items.title: ‘You Haven’t Got a Business Yet, You’ve Got a Theory’: Dave Ramsey to 25-Year-Old Working 3 Jobs
items.summary: A 25-year-old juggling three jobs asked Dave Ramsey whether to bet his entire savings on a fitness coaching brand before landing a single client. The answer exposed a mistake that quietly kills most side hustles before they ever start.

items.title: ‘Somebody Dangled a Carrot and Now You’re the Horse’: Ramsey to 21-Year-Old Eyeing $198K Sales Job
items.summary: A 21-year-old HVAC tech called Dave Ramsey four days before his wedding holding a cousin's promise of $198,000 and no benefits, and Ramsey's answer managed to praise sales as the fastest path to the C-suite while telling him to turn the offer down.

items.title: ‘You Don’t Have a $1,000 Problem, You Have a $104,000 Problem’: Dave Ramsey to Law Grad Eyeing Refi
items.summary: A new law grad called Dave Ramsey live to ask about refinancing her student loans, and his response reframed the entire question in a way that exposes the mistake most borrowers make before they ever talk to a lender.

items.title: C3.ai (AI) Posts 73% Bookings Growth As Free Cash Flow Turns Positive
items.summary: C3.ai (NYSE:AI) reported strong Q1 FY27 results with 73% quarter on quarter bookings growth and a return to positive free cash flow. The company signed 22 new high profile customer agreements in the quarter, including Ford and multiple U.S. government agencies. Federal sector bookings rose 138% year on year, while prior restructuring efforts contributed to steadier revenue and an improved operating loss profile. items.title: Chinese carmakers triple market share in a year
items.summary: Chinese brands have more than tripled their share of the British car market as drivers abandon Western marques for cheaper motors.

items.title: Ford’s 5.5% Yield Comes With One Big Warning
items.summary: Ford shareholders are collecting a 5.51% yield right now, but there is a reason income investors with long memories are watching this payout far more closely than the headline number suggests.

items.title: Volkswagen Aims to Revive U.S. Business
items.summary: President Trump’s tariff and electric-vehicle policies are colliding with Volkswagen’s plans for the large and lucrative U.S. market.  The WSJ’s Stephen Wilmot reports that  Volkswagen  is shaking up its U.S. leadership for the second time in two years as the world’s second-largest carmaker aims to revive its American business.  Veteran executive  Marco Schubert  will take over Volkswagen’s business in North America in October.

items.title: BMW Stock Has Rarely Been Cheaper Amid Pressure in Chinese Market
items.summary: The German car maker has an impeccable balance sheet and a great new electric-vehicle platform. Its profit margins should rebound.
